tool.name: FAIRe mapper: apply mapping
tool.description: write a FAIRe workbook from a sample sheet and its crosswalk
tool.command: #set $table_name = str($table.element_identifier).replace("'", "") #set $crosswalk_name = str($crosswalk.element_identifier).replace("'", "") python '$__tool_directory__/faire_mapper_apply.py' @TABLE_ARGS@ --crosswalk '$crosswalk' --checklist '$__tool_directory__/checklist/FAIRe_checklist_v1.0.2.xlsx' --template '$__tool_directory__/checklist/FAIRe_checklist_v1.0.2_FULLtemplate.xlsx' --assay_type '$assay_type' #if $sample_types: --sample_types '$sample_types' #end if --project_id '$project_id' #if str($assay_name).strip(): --assay_name '$assay_name' #end if #if str($country).strip(): --country '$country' #end if --date_order '$date_order' #if str($utc_offset).strip(): '--utc_offset=$utc_offset' #end if $include_review #if $project_values: --project_values '$project_values' #end if #if $req_lev: --req_lev 'M,$req_lev' #else: --req_lev 'M' #end if $drop_unmapped #for $o in $otu_tables: #set $oname = str($o.otu.element_identifier).replace("'", "") --otu '$o.otu' --otu_name '$oname' --otu_sheet '$o.otu_sheet' --otu_assay '$o.otu_assay' --otu_run '$o.otu_run' --otu_assay_column '$o.otu_assay_column' --otu_curated_column '$o.otu_curated_column' --otu_lineage '$o.otu_lineage' --otu_stage '$o.otu_stage' --otu_layout '$o.otu_layout' #if $o.otu_sequences: #set $sname = str($o.otu_sequences.element_identifier).replace("'", "") --otu_sequences '$o.otu_sequences' --otu_sequences_name '$sname' #else: --otu_sequences '' --otu_sequences_name '' #end if #if $o.taxa: --taxa '$o.taxa' --taxa_sheet '$o.taxa_sheet' #else: --taxa '' --taxa_sheet '' #end if #end for #for $l in $library_tables: #set $lname = str($l.library.element_identifier).replace("'", "") --library '$l.library' --library_name '$lname' --library_sheet '$l.library_sheet' --library_assay '$l.library_assay' --library_filter '$l.library_filter' --library_run '$l.library_run' #end for --table_name '$table_name' --crosswalk_name '$crosswalk_name' --output faire.xlsx --log '$log'

param.name: crosswalk
param.label: Crosswalk
param.help: The crosswalk (SSSOM) from FAIRe mapper: propose mapping, after review; edited in a spreadsheet and saved as Excel, CSV or tab-separated text is fine. Rows marked skos:exactMatch are applied: accepted, confirmed and model matches. To confirm a match for review, change its skos:closeMatch to skos:exactMatch. To stop a column being matched, delete its row; the column is then kept as a user-defined field unless you tick the option below to leave such columns out.

param.name: sample_types
param.label: Sample types
param.help: Leaves out the FAIRe fields specific to other sample types. Tick none to include all.

param.name: project_id
param.label: Project ID
param.help: A short identifier with no spaces, as FAIRe asks (letters, digits, _ or -).

param.name: assay_name
param.label: Assay name(s)
param.help: Separate several with commas, for example MiFish, crust16S. With one assay, the name is written to projectMetadata and to every sample; with several, each gets a column in projectMetadata, as FAIRe-ator makes them.

validator.message: Use letters, digits, _ or - in names, separated by commas

param.name: country
param.label: Country or sea for geo_loc_name (optional)
param.help: Put first in geo_loc_name when no column of the table gives a country or sea, for example Australia or Coral Sea Islands (INSDC names).

validator.message: Letters, spaces, commas, brackets, apostrophes and hyphens only

param.name: date_order
param.label: Dates such as 06/09/2017
param.help: Used only when no date in a column settles it (a value such as 13/09/2017 can only be day first).

param.name: utc_offset
param.label: UTC offset of the times of collection (optional)
param.help: When your table gives the time of collection in its own column (matched to verbatimEventTime), the tool joins each time to its date in eventDate, as FAIRe asks for the date and time of sampling. Give the offset of the local time from UTC, such as +10:00 for Australian Eastern Standard Time or +11:00 for Australian Eastern Daylight Time, so the time is unambiguous. eventDate keeps the local time, as daily cycles follow it: if the column name says the times are UTC, the tool converts them to local time with this offset. Leave empty to write local times without an offset.

validator.message: An offset such as +11:00, -04:00 or Z

param.name: include_review
param.label: Also apply the matches for review (skos:closeMatch)
param.help: Use this for a first draft. The log lists every match applied, so you can check them.

param.name: project_values
param.label: Values for the whole project (optional)
param.help: Things true of the whole study, such as the primers, extraction kit or sequencing platform: a table (Excel, CSV or tab-separated) with the columns term (a FAIRe term name) and value, and optionally status and assay. Rows whose status is not supported or confirmed are left out. A project-level term goes to projectMetadata; a sample-level term is written for every sample. With several assays, a row with an assay name goes to that assay's column of projectMetadata (primers or target gene, say). A column of your sample table takes precedence.

param.name: req_lev
param.label: Requirement levels to include
param.help: Mandatory fields are always included.

param.name: drop_unmapped
param.label: Leave out columns that are not matched to a FAIRe term
param.help: By default, a column with no skos:exactMatch row in the crosswalk (no row, or a skos:closeMatch row not confirmed) is kept as a user-defined field at the end of sampleMetadata, as FAIRe allows.

repeat.name: otu_tables
repeat.title: OTU or ASV table
repeat.help: Reads per sequence (or per taxon) and sample, one table per assay. Sample names must match the samp_name column (or lib_id).

param.name: otu
param.label: OTU or ASV table
param.help: Samples as columns (one row per ASV, with its ID or its sequence first; taxonomy and sequence columns may follow the counts), or samples as rows (one column per ASV or taxon, as in a published matrix of reads per taxon; sample details after the counts are left out).

param.name: otu_sheet
param.label: Excel sheet (OTU table)
param.help: Leave empty for the first sheet.

param.name: otu_layout
param.label: Layout of this table
param.help: Leave on Detect it unless the log says the table was read the wrong way round. Your choice then overrides the detection.
param.option: Samples as columns (one row per sequence or taxon)
Samples as rows (one row per sample)
Long form (one row per sample and sequence)

param.name: otu_assay
param.label: Assay of this table
param.help: One of the assay names above. Needed when several assays are named.

param.name: otu_assay_column
param.label: Column that gives each row's assay (optional)
param.help: For a table that holds several assays, such as Wilderlab's (its column target): one table is written for each assay, named by the column's values. Leave the assay of this table empty. If the assay names above are empty too, they are taken from this column.

param.name: otu_run
param.label: Sequencing run ID (seq_run_id) (optional)
param.help: Used when the table has no library or run columns: the tool then writes one experimentRunMetadata row per sample of this table, with samp_name, assay_name and this run ID, and lib_id made from those three.

param.name: otu_sequences
param.label: Sequences of this table (FASTA, optional)
param.help: For a table that names its sequences (ASV_1, ASV_2 ...) but does not hold them, such as an LCA output: a FASTA file whose headers are those names. FAIRe needs each sequence (dna_sequence in taxaRaw and taxaFinal). Sequences in the FASTA file that the table does not list are left out.

param.name: taxa
param.label: Taxonomy table (optional)
param.help: One row per ASV or OTU, keyed by its ID (or its sequence): FAIRe columns (kingdom ... specificEpithet, scientificName), rank columns (Kingdom ... Species, as DADA2 writes), or one lineage column (k__Animalia; p__Chordata ...). Taxonomy columns in the OTU table itself are read too; with neither, names in a table of reads per taxon are used.

param.name: otu_lineage
param.label: Lineage column to use (optional)
param.help: When the table has several lineage columns, such as PR2 tax and Silva 138.1 tax, the one that gives the taxonomy. Leave empty for the first; the others are kept in identificationRemarks.

param.name: otu_curated_column
param.label: Column of curated names (optional)
param.help: For an ASV table with a column giving each ASV's curated name. The tool uses your curated names; it does not curate. On its own, such a table is written twice, as FAIRe asks: as the raw tables, with every ASV, and as the final tables, where taxaFinal has a row for each ASV that has a curated name, and otuFinal sums the reads of each name under its most abundant ASV. ASVs left without a curated name (those removed in curation, such as off-target or contaminant sequences) stay in the raw tables only. If your curated names are in a separate table (for example one that holds only the curated ASVs), also provide the ASV table before curation as another OTU table, written as "otuRaw and taxaRaw", and set this table's "Write this table as" to "otuFinal and taxaFinal". This table then gives only the final tables, and each ASV's sequence comes from the raw table.

param.name: otu_stage
param.label: Write this table as
param.help: FAIRe keeps both: the tables before filtering and curation (raw) and the final tables. Add the same assay twice to give both, such as an ASV table as raw and its curated table as final. A final table without sequences takes them from the raw table, for rows with the same seq_id and the same reads (or fewer).

repeat.name: library_tables
repeat.title: Library table
repeat.help: Which sequence files belong to which sample: the run report of your study from ENA or the SRA, the SRA submission sheet, or your own run sheet. Fills experimentRunMetadata with lib_id, filename and filename2, their checksums, and associatedSequences (links to the run, BioSample and BioProject).

param.name: library
param.label: Library table
param.help: From ENA: the study's read_run file report (TSV), with library_name, run_accession, sample_accession, study_accession, fastq_ftp and fastq_md5 (or submitted_ftp and submitted_md5). From the SRA: RunInfo, or the SRA submission sheet. Your own sheet: columns such as sample name, library ID, filename, filename2 and md5, or a list of fastq files, one per line (a folder listing, md5sum's output or PowerShell's Get-FileHash CSV too), which the tool pairs by R1 and R2. Each library is matched to a sample by a sample name column, or by a library name that starts with the sample name (M159_16SFish matches M159).

param.name: library_sheet
param.label: Excel sheet (library table)
param.help: Leave empty for the first sheet that names libraries or files.

param.name: library_assay
param.label: Assays of these libraries
param.help: One or more of the assay names above, separated by commas. A library that holds the amplicons of two assays gets one row for each, each with its own lib_id. Needed when several assays are named.

validator.message: Letters, digits, _ or - in names, separated by commas

param.name: library_filter
param.label: Only the libraries whose name holds (optional)
param.help: For example 16SFish, to keep the 16S libraries of a report that lists every library of the study. Not case sensitive.

param.name: library_run
param.label: Sequencing run ID (seq_run_id) (optional)
param.help: Used when the table has no run column. Otherwise the run ID of the OTU table of the same assay is used.

tool.help:
@EARLY_VERSION@ **What it does**
This tool writes a FAIRe metadata workbook from your table and the crosswalk made by **FAIRe mapper: propose mapping**, which is the table, checked by you, that pairs each column of your table with a FAIRe term. The workbook has the same layout that FAIRe-ator makes (README, projectMetadata, sampleMetadata, the sheets for the assay type, and the drop-down values), so it can go straight to **FAIRe-fier** for checking and then on to the submission tools.
The tool writes each mapped column to its FAIRe term. Where FAIRe needs values in a set form, it converts them:
- **Dates** become ISO 8601 dates, so 12-Feb-19 becomes 2019-02-12. If a column's dates could be read either day first or month first (06/09/2017), the tool stops unless you tell it which. A single value such as 13/09/2017 settles it for the whole column. The dates as written are kept in verbatimEventDate, FAIRe's term for the date before formatting, unless a column of the table gives it. Dates stored as Excel date cells have no text to keep. - **Durations** become ISO 8601 durations: "2 days" becomes P2D, and 316 under a header such as *Days frozen* becomes P316D. - **A number and its unit** in one cell ("1 L") are split between the term and its unit term (samp_size and samp_size_unit). Where the term has a set unit, the tool keeps just the number, so "0.2 micron" for size_frac becomes 0.2, and millimetres are converted to µm. - **Place names in several columns** are combined into geo_loc_name, in the order given in the crosswalk: "Australia: Great Barrier Reef, Lizard Island". If no column gives the country, set it on the form. - **Latitude and longitude in one cell** (MIxS lat_lon, "40.57773667 S 148.7301917 E") are split into decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude, with south and west written as negative numbers. - **Yes/no** values become 1 and 0, allowed values take the checklist's spelling, and country names take the INSDC spelling. A yes/no column that marks the controls (``value_part`` *negative control if yes*) is written to samp_category as *negative control* or *sample*. - **Dates saved with a time of midnight** (2023-06-30 00:00:00, as Excel and many scripts save them) are written as dates only. - **"missing: not collected" in a control** (a negative or positive control, or a PCR standard) is written as "not applicable: control sample", which is FAIRe's term for a value that a control does not have. - **A column with one value for a project-level term** is written once, to projectMetadata.
Columns with no ``skos:exactMatch`` row are kept as user-defined fields, as FAIRe allows, unless you tick *Leave out columns that are not matched to a FAIRe term*.
@HELP_INPUTS@
-----
**Inputs**
- **Your table**, as you gave it to *propose mapping*. - **Crosswalk**: the SSSOM crosswalk from *propose mapping*. The tool applies the rows marked ``skos:exactMatch``, which are the accepted, confirmed and model matches. It leaves out the rows marked for review (``skos:closeMatch``) unless you tick the option to apply them. You can edit the crosswalk to confirm a match (change ``skos:closeMatch`` to ``skos:exactMatch``), to change the term (``object_label``), or to stop a column being matched (delete its row).
Two columns of the crosswalk say how to build values. ``combine_order`` numbers the columns that together make geo_loc_name; edit it to change the order of the parts. ``value_part`` says which part of each cell a term takes: the number or the unit of "1 L", the latitude or the longitude of a MIxS lat_lon, or *negative control if yes*. A column can have several rows, one for each term it fills, so one depth column fills both minimumDepthInMeters and maximumDepthInMeters. - **Project ID, assay names, sample types and requirement levels**, as in FAIRe-ator. - **Values for the whole project** (optional): a table with the columns ``term`` and ``value``, and optionally ``status`` and ``assay``, such as the values found in the methods text. Only rows with the status *supported* or *confirmed*, or with no status, are applied. With several assays, a row that gives an assay name (as given in *Assay name(s)*) goes to that assay's column of projectMetadata. This means values that differ between assays, such as the primers and the target gene, each sit with their own assay. Rows without an assay go to project_level. - **OTU or ASV tables** (optional; one per assay, or two per assay, raw and final). These hold the reads of each sequence or taxon in each sample.
The tool works out whether the samples are columns or rows from the sample names, which must match samp_name or lib_id, or be their Illumina file names (M108_S7_L001 for M108), or carry a prefix that every sample column has (S_M108 for M108). If the log says a table was read the wrong way round, set its *Layout of this table*.
A table in long form, with one row per sample and sequence (and columns such as *sample*, *ASV* and *reads*), is turned into one row per sequence. Counts on repeated rows are added together, and columns that vary within a sequence are left out. A table that holds several assays, with a column giving each row's assay (Wilderlab's *target*), is split by that column (*Column that gives each row's assay*). A sample column that appears twice is used once, with a warning. A name given with its rank (NCBI's names and ranks, as Wilderlab gives them) fills its rank term. *root* means no assignment, so no name is written, and *unclassified Paracalanus* is named Paracalanus.
With the samples as columns, the first column is the ASV ID or the sequence itself (as DADA2 writes it), and taxonomy, confidence and sequence columns may follow the counts. With the samples as rows (a published matrix of reads per taxon, say), the counts end at the first column that is not counts or that names a sample detail (*Site depth*), and the columns from there on are left out. Empty cells are written as 0. - **Taxonomy table** (optional, one for each OTU table). This can hold FAIRe columns, rank columns (Kingdom ... Species) or a lineage column (``k__Animalia; p__Chordata; ...``), and is keyed by the ASV ID or its sequence.
FAIRe's rank terms (kingdom to species) are Linnaean ranks, so the tool fills them fully only for Linnaean classifications, such as NCBI or BOLD taxonomy, whose names typically carry Linnaean ranks. Lineages from PR2 and SILVA without rank labels, as mothur and the Wang classifier write them (``Eukaryota(100);Obazoa(100);...``), are read by position. From SILVA the tool takes the phylum to genus, and from PR2 only the genus and species, since PR2's levels in between are not Linnaean ranks (its class can be Arthropoda, for example). An ASV named only above genus in PR2 gets that name as scientificName, with taxonRank *other: PR2 division* (or another PR2 level), and identificationRemarks on each PR2 row says that PR2 was used. Add the PR2 version you used (for example PR2 v5.0.0) as otu_db in your values for the whole project.
Placeholders such as *Dinophyta_XX*, *Calanoida_fa* or *_unclassified* are skipped, and the classifier's confidence for the name given becomes confidence_score. The lineage itself is kept in verbatimIdentification. If there are several lineage columns, the first (or the one named on the form) gives the taxonomy, and the others are kept in identificationRemarks.
A name column (scientificName, or a curated name such as *New_Name*) gives the rank too. Binomials are species, and names such as *Trachurus Sp* or *Diaphus Sp1* are named to their first word (the genus Trachurus) and kept as written in verbatimIdentification. A name that reads as a common name (*Atlantic Salmon*) is kept in verbatimIdentification, the rank columns name the taxon, and the log lists it for you to check. With no taxonomy, the tool uses the names in a table of reads per taxon: binomials as species, names ending in -idae as families, -iformes as orders, and other single words as genera. - **Raw and final tables.** FAIRe keeps the tables from before curation (*otuRaw*, *taxaRaw*) and after it (*otuFinal*, *taxaFinal*). The raw tables hold every ASV. taxaFinal lists every ASV of the final taxa, one per row, and otuFinal sums the reads of each taxon's ASVs under the ID of its most abundant ASV.
The simplest input for these four tables is an ASV table with a column that gives each ASV's curated name (*Column of curated names*). From that one table, the tool writes otuRaw, taxaRaw, otuFinal and taxaFinal. You can also give the assay two OTU tables: the ASV table, written as otuRaw and taxaRaw, and a curated table with one row per taxon, written as otuFinal and taxaFinal (set with *Write this table as* for each). Each final row then takes the sequence of the ASV it is named after from the raw table. A row with more reads than that ASV holds several ASVs. In that case identificationRemarks says so, and the log asks for the curated name of each ASV so that taxaFinal can list them all.
If your curated names are in a separate ASV table, such as one of the curated ASVs only and without sequences, give it as final with its *Column of curated names*, and the ASV table before curation as raw. The final tables then come from the curated table, and each ASV's sequence from the raw table.
When neither the table nor a library table gives the libraries, the tool writes one experimentRunMetadata row for each sample of each OTU table, with the assay name and the run ID you give, and samp_name standing in for the library name in lib_id (see below). - **Library tables** (optional). These say which sequence files belong to which sample. You can give the run report of your study from ENA (the *read_run* file report: on the study's ENA page, choose the columns library_name, run_accession, sample_accession, study_accession, fastq_ftp and fastq_md5) or from the SRA (RunInfo), the SRA submission sheet, or your own run sheet. A plain list of your fastq files also works: one name per line, with or without a header, and an md5 column if you have the checksums. The checksum files that sequencing providers send (md5sum's output: the checksum, two spaces and the file name on each line) and the CSV that Windows PowerShell writes (``Get-FileHash -Algorithm MD5 *.fastq.gz | Export-Csv md5.csv``) are read as they are. The tool pairs the files by their read number (1A_16S_Fish_R1.fastq.gz and 1A_16S_Fish_R2.fastq.gz make library 1A_16S_Fish) and logs how many it paired. The tool matches each library to a sample by a sample name column, or by a library name that starts with the sample name (M159_16SFish_LerayCOI matches M159). Libraries of other samples are left out and listed in the log.
The tool writes one experimentRunMetadata row for each library and assay, with lib_id, filename and filename2, checksum_filename and checksum_filename2, and associatedSequences as links to the run, the BioSample and the BioProject. It also fills platform, lib_layout and checksum_method in projectMetadata when the libraries agree, and reports the instrument for you to add with its OBI ID. ENA's fastq_ftp files are ENA's copies of the reads, named after the run (SRR33695780_1.fastq.gz), with their own checksums; submitted_ftp and submitted_md5 give the files as you submitted them. The library tables take the place of the run columns in your table, but any values in those columns that the library tables do not give are kept. - **lib_id.** FAIRe defines a library as "an amplicon of a sample with unique MIDs", so each row of experimentRunMetadata is one amplicon of one sample in one sequencing run. The tool writes lib_id as the library name, the assay name and the run ID, joined by underscores (M097_16SFish_LerayCOI_Fish16S_AGRF_2024-12). When the library name already ends with the assay name, the assay is not repeated (1A_16S_Fish_AGRF_NovaSeq6000_SP). A library that holds the amplicons of several assays in one set of files, as in the SEA-MES 16S and COI data, gets a lib_id for each amplicon, and the rows share the files. The log lists such libraries. The names are long, but they are machine readable, and FAIRe2NCBI and FAIRe2ENA take the assay and run off again so that the archives get the library's own name. - **A file in the wrong field.** If a file given as an OTU, taxonomy or library table looks like another kind of file, the run stops or warns, and says what the file looks like and which field it belongs in. It also warns when a table written as final has more sequences or reads than the raw table of the same assay, as happens when *Write this table as* is set the wrong way round. **FAIRe mapper: identify your files** can tell you what each of your files is before you start.
**Outputs**
- **FAIRe workbook** (.xlsx). The OTU and taxonomy tables are added as *otuFinal* and *taxaFinal*, or as *otuRaw* and *taxaRaw*, as set for each table. When there are several assays, the assay name is added to the sheet names (*otuFinal_MiFish*), as in the FAIRe examples. - **Log**. This lists the inputs; each column written, with the conversion and an example; the values for the whole project; **commonly confused terms** given in those values (such as samp_size and samp_vol_we_dna_ext), each with the terms it is confused with and how to tell them apart; what was left out and why; warnings, such as values that could not be converted or repeated sample names; and the **mandatory terms still empty**, which are the next things to fill in.

**Not yet done by this tool**
- The tool does not look up the ranks above a name. For a table of reads per taxon, use **edna2obis: match taxa** to fill them from WoRMS or GBIF. ``dna_sequence`` stays empty when neither the table nor a raw table of the same assay gives it. - Cell comments are not added to the sheets. Drop-down lists are added, in the same way FAIRe-ator adds them, from the *Drop-down values* sheet. - ``checkls_ver`` is kept as written when you give it (in the values for the whole project, or a column): a number stays a number, and text such as v2.0.0 stays text. If you do not give it, it is written as the checklist defines it. FAIRe checklist v1.0.2 defines it as a number, so it is written as 1, as the FAIRe examples have it; a checklist that defines it as text (FAIRe v2) gets the full version, such as v2.0.0, from the checklist's file name. Text given for a checklist that defines a number is kept, and the log warns that FAIRe-fier will report it. The README sheet names the exact checklist (*FAIRe_checklist_v1.0.2.xlsx*). FAIRe-ator writes the file name here, which FAIRe-fier reports as an error. - Values from the table and the methods text are written to *project_level*. For values that differ between assays, add an ``assay`` column to the values for the whole project, or move the values to the assay columns yourself.
